What Module 104 covers

Unit 350 liquefies the treated gas against a mixed refrigerant compressed by six identical trains, PK-351-1 to PK-351-6, each a two-stage LP + HP oil-flooded screw set on its own P&ID sheet, PR13 to PR18. Five run, one stands by.

  • Walk the MR loop in flow order and say what each stream is doing — compression, precooling, condensing, letting down, boiling back.
  • Name the six trains and their two stages, and say why the plant runs five of six and what the standby is for.
  • Read the lube-oil system as one inventory with two loops and two machines, not as a list of parts.
  • Watch the right numbers. The unit carries 317 instrument tags; know the handful that are protections rather than indications.
  • Take it through start-up and shutdown — the permissives before the sequence, and the overlap at shutdown you must not interrupt.

Block 1 · principle — HMB rev 7 case C1S · Manual §8.4 · GC datasheet AT-3581 (TAM-158-RFQ-GC_02, 2025-04-16) · NH₃ MSDS via Module 103

Why a mixed refrigerant — the cooling curve

Schematic. End points are the C1S design case (F16 +14.77, F19 −149, M1 +0.66, M11/M12 −161.183 °C); the shape between them is drawn for legibility — no composite curve for this plant exists. Composition AT-3581; the nC4 cut may be i-butane, the GC reads both.
  • Gas does not condense at one temperature. The feed is itself a mixture — 89.54 % C1, 8.84 % N₂ (HMB, F16) — so it gives up its heat over a glide: +14.77 down to −149 °C, 164 K, 2 650 kW (DERIVED).
  • A pure fluid does. Ammonia proves it on our own plant: into E-354 at 1.896 °C, out at 1.0 °C — the whole evaporator moves less than 1 K. A flat line under a sloping one is wasted work.
  • A mixture boils over a range. The LP MR leaves V-355B at −161.183 °C and reaches the compressor at +0.66 °C — one fluid across 162 K, absorbing 14 448 kW (DERIVED).
  • So the two curves run parallel. A small approach everywhere: the whole gas duty on one exchanger and one compression loop, instead of a cascade of three fluids and three sets of machines.
why not ammoniaThe ammonia of Module 103 cannot do this job. It boils at −33 °C and freezes at −77.7 °C (NH₃ MSDS) — no pressure takes it to −149 °C. Here it is a pre-cooler only: E-354 takes the HP MR from 55 to 5 °C and condenses 22.5 mol % of it (DERIVED) for 4 318 kW. Everything below 5 °C is the MR.
Block 1 · the fluid — P&ID PR19 (S-357) rev 5 · PR20 rev 6 · PR11 rev 6 AFC · Manual Table 8.3

The MR itself — four components, and the train that keeps it dry

Storages, the four XEV tags, the driers, the after filter and V-358 are PR19 and PR20; the arrangement is ours. Colours are the four components of slide 08, same warm-to-cold order.
the make-up side · PR19The make-up side is a 10 barg family — the loop it feeds is not. Both bullets V-357-3 / V-357-4 and the common 1½″ header are 10 barg, and make-up enters at V-358, the lowest pressure point of the loop. PR19 note ① also allows either bullet to be charged by hose. • PR19 note ②: client shall supply the LNG tank for first filling.
Maintenancethe molecular sieve in V-359A/B is replaced every 2 years — no running-hour limit, the calendar is the whole rule. The procedure writes the tag V-35A/B; the canonical tag is the one above.F-359 cartridges: 2 years or ΔP > 0.7 bar, whichever comes first. That is the only way a saturated sieve or a dusting bed shows up before the cold box does the finding for you.21044-MN-PRO-00001 Rev.00 §6.6

Mixed refrigerant hazards — flammable, cryogenic, asphyxiant

1 · It burns
GHS02 · H220
extremely flammable gas
  • LNG vapour burns from 4 vol % up to 15
  • Autoignition 537 °C · a hot surface is enough
  • Cold vapour is heavier than air below −107 °C — it pools
2 · It freezes
GHS04 · H281
refrigerated gas
  • Cryogenic burns from liquid, cold vapour and cold metal
  • LNG boils at −162 °C · liquid to gas about 625 : 1
  • Flush with 38–41 °C water · never rub
3 · It takes the air
no GHS pictogram
exists for this
  • Not toxic. It displaces the oxygen, and that is enough
  • TLV 1 000 ppm TWA for C1 and C2 · simple asphyxiant
  • Below 19.5 % O₂ it is SCBA — a filter does nothing
Mixed refrigerant is odourless at every concentration. Nothing tells you it is there — and the cold vapour runs along the ground looking for an ignition source.Not toxic is not the same as not dangerous · the gas detectors are the only nose this unit has
What is in it
  • C2 42.25 · C1 29.30 · nC4 19.11 · N₂ 9.34 mol %
  • GC sheet for AT-3581 · 31.13 kg/kmol, the HMB agrees
  • No flammability limit for this mixture is stated anywhere
What stands in for your nose
  • 14 gas detectors and 2 flame · the F&G layout places 12, one on every PK-351 train
  • 20 % LEL pre-alarm · 40 % LEL shuts the unit down, 1ooN
  • TALL-3561 cold box basin — the only cryogenic-spill alarm
If it escapes
  • Gas horn and blue beacon at CB-356 — evacuate, then kill every ignition source
  • Wind sock at V-357-4 · stay upwind and uphill, out of low ground
  • The visible cloud is not the boundary — gas is outside it
ISO 7010 W021
flammable material
ISO 7010 P003
no flame, no ignition source
ISO 7010 M047
use breathing equipment
ISO 7010 E002
emergency exit
Safety · cold — LNG SDS 2015001 §4 / §5 / §6 / §9 · Manual §8.7 p165 · P&ID PR11 · PR12 · PR13 · PR20 · PR22 · HMB rev 7 case 1 summer

Cryogenic safety — cold burns, brittle steel, spills and oxygen

Cold metal looks exactly like warm metal, and cryogenic liquid trapped between two closed valves has nowhere to go.On this unit the answer to the second one is thermal relief — TSV-3572 / TSV-3573, set at 5 barg, on the LNG line to V-221
Cold burns
  • Liquid, cold vapour, cold metal
  • Flush with lukewarm water, 38–41 °C
  • Never rub · no hot water, no dry heat
Brittle fracture
  • Carbon steel loses toughness when cold
  • It does not bend — it breaks, no warning
  • Never spill a cryogen on structural steel
Spill behaviour
  • Liquid to gas, about 625 : 1
  • The white cloud is not the hazard edge
  • No water on it — it boils faster
Oxygen
  • CB-356 is N₂-purged · breather 7.5 mbarg
  • T-357 overhead 51.8 % N₂ / 48.2 % CH₄
  • Under 19.5 % O₂ it is SCBA, not a filter

General practice, not a plant rule: brittle fracture, the trapped-liquid rule and rapid phase transition — a cryogen on water flashing with no combustion. Inside CB-356 — what a brazed-aluminium plate-fin exchanger is

Textbook plate-fin geometry. No internal drawing of either exchanger exists in the document set.
  • Stacked layers, brazed into one block. Corrugated aluminium fins between flat parting sheets, closed at the edges by side bars; the stack is dip-brazed in a vacuum furnace into a single piece of metal. Headers and nozzles are welded on afterwards — no joints inside, no gaskets anywhere.
  • Multistream. One block, several fluids, each with its own layers. E-356B has ten nozzles: six MR and four gas. The MR passes twice (C down, condensing; D up, evaporating) and the gas passes twice (B2, then B3 after the NGL knock-out in V-356B).
  • It is never opened. No removable bundle, no tube to rod, no gasket — and it sits in a perlite-filled box that would have to be emptied first. The only in-situ tools the drawings give you are the core thermocouples TT-3562A…Y for a controlled cool-down (PR11 note ③) and a nitrogen defrost (note ④).
  • Oil carry-over is what kills it. At −157 °C compressor oil is a solid. It plates out in millimetre-high passages and there is no way to get it out. Manual §8.4: a common mechanical oil removal system, S-352, … provides cryogenic-grade oil separation to protect the plate-fin heat exchangers. S-352 is not housekeeping — it is what keeps the cold box alive.
BlockWhat it doesDesign dutyMaterials and design conditions
E-356A gas-gas PFHEFeed gas against the gas expanded across PV-3561A. What −75 °C is protecting
  • C5-plus does not condense down there — it FREEZES and plugs a plate-fin channel nobody can open, clean or inspect.
  • So: drop to −75 °C, knock the condensate out in V-356B, send only clean vapour to the B3 pass.
  • V-356A / V-356B · 24" · aluminium · 0.63 m³ · no internals · inside the box · liquid out under LV-3561A/B to E-371.

Block 2 · nitrogen rejection — Manual §8.1 / §8.4 · P&ID PR12 rev 7 AS BUILT · HMB C1S

The NRU (1) — why the nitrogen has to come out, and what T-357 is

The three streams are HMB rev 7 case C1S (F20 / F22 / F24) on one common nitrogen scale; T-357 and X-357 are the symbols of P&ID PR12 rev 7 AS BUILT, traced from the drawing and not redrawn by us. The routing of the lines and the labels are ours.
why the nitrogen has to come out
  • Product quality. Manual §8.1 states the duty of the unit in one line: NRU distillation column (T-357) achieving LNG N₂ ≤ 1.1 mol % — the only product-quality figure in the whole of §8.
  • Heating value. Nitrogen is inert. Every mole of it in the LNG is a mole that does not burn — it dilutes the calorific value of the cargo. Boil-off too: nitrogen is more volatile than methane, so it leaves the liquid first and fills the tank vapour space. Principle — no plant figure for it exists in our sources.
  • And it is not vented. Manual Table 8.1: the nitrogen-rich overhead goes to the fuel gas system, through E-372, the NRU vaporizer in Unit 370. It is burned, not lost.
T-357 — a reboiled stripper, not a full column
  • Table 8.3 names it N2 STRIPPER. Random packing, no condenser and no reflux — nothing comes back down the top. 20″ NPS Sch 10S · 7 620 mm TL-TL · SS304 · 1.5 m³ · 10 barg · −180/65 °C · insulation 150 mm.
  • The flash is what separates. The let-down across CV-3551 drops the LNG from 37.85 to 2.50 barg; 7.28 % of it vaporises and the nitrogen goes with that vapour.
  • X-357 does the rest. The reboiler keeps boiling the bottoms so the nitrogen still dissolved in the liquid is driven back up through the packing — which is why the bottoms come out warmer than the feed.
Block 2 · nitrogen rejection — P&ID PR12 rev 7 AS BUILT · Manual §8.4 · Tables 8.9 / 8.10 · HMB C1S

The NRU (2) — the electric reboiler, the two outlets, and the spec

The equipment outline is the PRO13-ING-PR12 rev 7 AS BUILT symbol itself, lifted from the drawing and rescaled — column, kettle, the 20″ flange between them, the element head and the dished right head are all PR12 geometry. The packing, the boiling pool at NLL 180 mm of the 1 000 mm ID and every callout are drawn on top. Stream F30 is HMB rev 7 case C1S; the instrument systems and junction boxes are the TAM instrument index. Both level instruments carry 22xx tags inside Unit 350 — they belong to the V-221 numbering, not a typing error.
X-357 — N₂ rejection reboilerP&ID PR12 · electric
typeHorizontal electric kettle · the column stands on it, N3 20″#150
rated power90 kW · 690 Vac-50Hz-3 · H 8″#150 element · turn down by SCR
bodySS304 · Ø1 000 ID × SM-SM 5 000 mm · 10 barg · −180/65 °C · insulation C 170 mm
levelsHHLL 450 · HLL 380 · NLL 180 · LLL 110 · LLLL 80 mm · glass LG-2211
what the drawing is telling you
  • Two kinds of control, and the drawing says why. No condenser, so the overhead is held on pressure; the bottoms go to the tank, so they are held on level. Both valves fail closed.
  • Control and protection share neither instrument nor box. LT-2211 → PCS box P-PN-CB357.1 → LIC-2211. LT-2212 → ESD box E-PN-CB357.1 → LAHH-2212 (PSD) and LALL-2212 (LSD). TAHH-X-357 is hardwired to the MCC.
  • Its own cold box. T-357 and X-357 are not inside CB-356: they sit in CB-357, a separate insulated enclosure downstream.
MaintenanceCB-357 and V-221 are static equipment: the procedure foresees no major maintenance activity for either of them. That is the whole plan — one line, and it is a deliberate one.21044-MN-PRO-00001 Rev.00 §6.6

(no valve of its own)		From those three it establishes balanced operating conditions for the refrigeration circuit, matching process cooling demand to the refrigeration actually available. Two operator-selectable modes: differential-pressure control and discharge-pressure control. The internal algorithm sits in the PCS and §8.4 declares it out of scope, so no tuning is published.
PIC-3561BThe single loop under that supervisor · holds gas pressure at the E-356B outlet (Table 8.9)PT-3561B · 0..50 bargPV-3561BIt strokes the valve. Its set point is written by XC-3561B when the supervisor is in service, and by the operator when it is not. No set point is published in any source — Table 8.9 leaves the cell empty.
PV-3561BThe final element — the MR let-down (Joule-Thomson) valve— (positioner · solenoid PEV-3561B on ESD)the MR process line into V-355B4 in, fail closed. It expands the cold high-pressure refrigerant into V-355B, and that expansion is what makes the cold box cold. It is outside the box, where you can reach it. Table 8.6 names it V-355B inlet pressure control, Table 8.9 names the loop by the E-356B outlet — two ends of one valve (A-22).
XC-3551Supervisory limiting function over the NRU feed and reboiler system — not a flow controllerTT-3551 cold-box outlet gas temperature
FT-3551 gas flow rate		CV-3551It admits gas to T-357 only when cold-box outlet conditions are inside the required range. If the temperature is not low enough — which means the cold box is not performing — CV-3551 is driven towards closed, to keep off-specification gas out of the column and protect what is downstream.

What the drawing is telling you
  • The HP does not see only the LP discharge. Its suction header is built from four streams — the 8in LP discharge, the 6in feed straight off the package suction, and two 3/4in oil returns from V-351-1. A slide-valve move on the LP changes what the HP breathes, not just how much.
  • Five of six carry the loop. 6 × 20 % — five trains make the whole MR flow, so the sixth is not spare capacity: it is what keeps the loop whole when one goes down.
  • One relief on the compressors, and it is on the interstage. PSV-3511.H1 · 28 barg, marked BLOCKED OUTLET. Sheet 1 carries no PSV at all, so the LP blocked-outlet protection is that same valve. XV-3511.1 is the one 12in valve that isolates the whole package.
  • PK-351-1 feeds instrument air to the whole row. One 1in line from Unit 500 lands here and is distributed to the other five packages — a single-point dependency, and it is on the P&ID.
  • Only the two emergency stops take a whole train down. Every process cause trips its own stage — Tables 8.12–8.17. Unit 340 tripped the whole package. The register holds no cause-and-effect for area 350.

Two stages — C-351L and C-351H

Train and tags PR13 sh.1 / sh.2 · states HMB C1S · order Tables 8.19 / 8.20 · nameplates PR13 sh.1 / sh.2 + plant_equipment · oil and 6 × 20 % vendor slide 38, single source. The ratio is arithmetic: (18.30 + 1.013) / (1.40 + 1.013) = 8.0. The arrangement is ours.
Block 3 · 3/10 · principle — GEA Grasso LT series · vendor slides 38 / 41 · PR13 sh.1 §2.1, sh.2 §3.1–3.4

How an oil-flooded screw compressor works

  • Two meshing helical rotors in a close-clearance cast-iron casing, 28 barg, −60 / 120 °C. Gas enters between the lobes at the suction end.
  • The pocket seals, then shrinks. It is cut off from suction and squeezed as it travels axially until it uncovers the discharge port. Vi 2.2 is how much it shrinks first.
  • Oil is injected into the compression space — nozzles B (main injection) and B1 (additional injection) on both machines. It seals the rotor clearances, cools the gas and lubricates the bearings.
  • So the discharge is an oil/gas mixture, not gas — 6"-MR-3511xx to V-351-x. The oil separator is the second half of the compressor, not an accessory. That is Block 4.
  • Positive displacement — no surge, no stall. Close the outlet and it keeps pumping until something fails. PR13 sheet 1 carries no PSV: the package has exactly one compressor relief, PSV-3511.H1 @ 28 barg, blocked-outlet case, on the interstage — which is the LP machine's own discharge.
  • Therefore capacity cannot be throttled with a valve. It is changed by the slide valve — next slide.

Block 3 · 4/10 · capacity control — ZT-3511.Lx / .Hx · ZEV-3511…3514 (Y1–Y4) · §8.7.1 · vendor slides 39–41

Capacity control — the slide valve

  • What it is: a block moving parallel to the rotor axis, changing the area of the opening in the bottom of the casing. It shortens the region of compression and returns the surplus gas to suction. More capacity → toward discharge; less → toward suction.
  • How it moves: hydraulically, on the compressor lube oil. No oil pressure, no capacity control — and no start. ΔP ≥ 1.5 bar checked, both valves driven < 5 %, before either motor turns.
  • Solenoids: ZEV-3511 / 3512 / 3513 / 3514, .Lx / .Hx, terminals Y1–Y4, Danfoss 018F4704 — four per machine, 48 in the unit, same part number as Unit 340. Vendor block 4: Y2+Y3 → pressure side; Y1+Y4 → suction side.
  • Feedback: ZT-3511.Lx / .Hx, 0–100 %, local indication ZI-3511.Lx. No ZC tag exists in any source — position is ZT only.
  • Who decides: the MR suction pressure, through PIC-3511.Hx per machine (and PIC-3511.Lx, live on the HMI, in no table and on no P&ID), set point cascaded from the master XC-3501A / B. The PLC also unloads on motor current — in two steps, on approach and hard above the limit.
  • What part load costs: §8.7.1 rates the slide valve above recycle or hot-gas bypass — but gas sent back to suction was already carried partway along the rotors, and that work is lost. Below the floor it cannot go lower — that is the next slide.

Why this one matters
  • Module 103 hands over here. Two 10in R1 TO PK-341, 4in R1 FROM V-343, 3in from V-341 — four crossings of the unit boundary on one drawing.
  • The only partial condensation in the loop: vapour fraction 1.00 → 0.775 at 5 °C, so 22.5 mol % (DERIVED) turns liquid here. V-355A and P-355A/B exist for it.

Where each phase goes
  • Vapour, straight through. Top nozzle, 10in-MR-350027-3L1-C35 to E-356B — it enters the cold box at hexagon CinV with nothing in between.
  • Liquid, pumped. Bottom nozzle to P-355A/B, then 4in-MR-000032-3L1-C30 to E-356B at hexagon CinL. The liquid road is the only one with a machine on it.
  • Two level valves, opposite jobs. LV-3550 exports liquid to the cold box (stream M8); LV-3551 with LEV-3551 recycles back into V-355A through RO-3550B / RO-3551B on the minimum-flow lines marked NO POCKETS.
  • Which controller strokes LV-3551 is in no source (C-06). Table 8.6 gives both valves the same service, V-355A liquid level control, and Table 8.9 lists only LIC-3550 → LV-3550. The topology above is settled by the UFD and PR22; the controller is left unstated.
V-355B · LP MR separator · inside the cold box · PR11
  • The other end of the same fluid. PV-3561B — outside the box — lets stream M10 down from 17.00 barg / −157 °C to 2.00 barg / −161.2 °C, flashing 7.2 mol %.
  • Register: 0.9 m³, 24in, aluminium, −196/65 °C. From there to compressor suction is 0.60 bar in total — and no document gives a value in between.

Oil separator internals — the coalescers and where the oil goes

V-351-x INTERNALS — two separation stages, two return legsPR13 sh.2 · vendor slides 27 / 28
  • Both legs go to the C-351H-x SUCTION, not back to the reservoir. Manual Table 8.6 gives XEV-3521.x and XEV-3522.x the same service text — that is not a copy-paste error, the legs really are parallel.
  • The needle valves are a one-time commissioning setting. Mis-operating them loses performance and increases oil carry-over. Check the glass, do not turn the valve.
  • Before opening: compressor shut down and vessel pumped down. Replace clogged elements, then retighten every element so the sealing is tight.
Vendor slide 28 — the coalescer section
What escapes the separator is not lost oil — it is the cold box's problem. Carry-over travels with the refrigerant and is taken out downstream by S-352 (slide 30), which returns it to the 20in suction header. Each package then educts it back through its own ejector EJ1-351.x, with sight glass SG-3514.x so you can see it working — that duty is the reading of PR13 sh.1, not a printed statement (assumption C-03).

Block 4 · 5/9 · the magnetic coupling — P-351-x · vendor slides 22 / 23 · Manual §8.7.6

The magnetic coupling — and its hazards

Vendor slide 22 — the two rotors and the shell between them
Three parts · the two halves never touch
PartMounted onWhat it does
Outer rotormotor MP-351-x shaftcarries the driving magnets
Containment shellstatic, between the twothis IS the shaft seal — no dynamic seal, no leak path
Inner rotorpump P-351-x shaftdragged round by the field across the shell
Vendor wording: the magnetic coupling serves as a shaft seal and for transmitting the torque — which is why a pump handling refrigerant-laden oil was given one.
When it lets go — and why it is silent
1 · OVERLOAD
Load rises above the maximum transmissible torque of the magnets.
2 · DECOUPLE
The magnets slip. The motor keeps turning; the pump stops pumping.
3 · NO SIGN
No noise, no visible change. Oil circulation is lost with nothing to hear. Dry running shall be strictly avoided.
4 · CAUGHT BY ΔP
PDI-3514.Lx / .Hx falls: below 1.5 barD the start is inhibited and a running compressor is tripped.
Strong magnetic field — the OEM distances
2 mDANGER · risk to lifeFor people with active implanted cardiac devices. Keep 2 m from unmounted coupling components and 0.5 m from installed couplings and the bell housing.
0.5 mWARNING · mutual attractionMagnetic or magnetisable parts are pulled together uncontrolled within this distance.
1 mATTENTION · data carriersDiscs, credit cards and badges are damaged within this distance.
⚠ Exercise extreme caution if the motor is removed for maintenance — the 2 m figure is for unmounted parts.

Tighten the flange bolts and return the housing to standby, ready for the next change.

Block 4 · 8/9 · heater, reliefs, equalisation — X-351-x · PSV-3517.x / PSV-3518.x · PEV-3511.x · Table 8.20 · conflict A-09

X-351-x oil heater, the two oil reliefs, PEV-3511.x equalisation

Vendor slide 24 — PSV-3518.x, the pump relief. S suction side · P pressure side. 3 is the compression spring and 4 the adjustment screw: this valve is set on a differential across itself, which is why its set point is 6 bar DIFF and not a gauge pressure.
Two reliefs — two different jobs
PSV-3517.xA / xB · change-over valve28 barg

Protects the SEPARATOR — the whole oil inventory, sitting at MR discharge pressure.

Relieves to the HOT flare header.

PSV-3518.x · the valve in the picture6 bar DIFF

Protects the PUMP only, from its own over-pressure.

Relieves back to the pump suction — it never sees the flare.

▤ X-351-x · the oil heater — PR13 sh.3 + §8.7.5
5.425kW · 690 Vac 3 ph
Elements inside V-351-x, nozzles H1 / H2, 4in each. It maintains oil temperature during shutdown and prevents refrigerant dilution in the lubricant — cold oil holds dissolved refrigerant, and diluted oil does not carry a bearing film. TT-3517.x → TIC-3517.x, ON-OFF to the heater and to nothing else.
A-19 · the oil temperature band this slide does NOT print
vendor pack60 / 40 °C
HMI faceplate16 / 18 °C
PR13 sh.3a bare ON-OFF
PEV-3511.x — the last step of a shutdown. Table 8.20: after post-lubrication the system commands CLOSE oil pressure equalisation valve and isolate the lubrication circuit. On PR13 sh.2 the same device is the solenoid pilot on PCV-3511.x, the 4in × 3in regulator that feeds the LP oil header — one device, two names. Not to be confused with the 3/4in MR equalising line that bleeds the isolated, warming suction spool back to the header when XV-3511.x is shut. One line of honesty: Table 8.20 commands that close twice, once for LP and once for HP, while the drawing carries one PEV-3511.x per package, on the LP header.

Valves — relief, control, solenoid, shutdown

Unit 350 — valves by family, drawn as they are builtyellow = SAFETY only · solenoid box = on/off · diaphragm = control · spring = relief
183 instrumented valve assets = 100 solenoids + 47 relief + 24 control + 12 on/off. plant_valves holds 170 rows; the 13-row gap is the fifteen self-contained regulators, which live in plant_instruments, less the PEV-3540 row that is stored twice — once as a PCS branch and once as an ESD branch, on one physical solenoid (CR-00121 is open on whether the two outputs are in series). Where the register and the drawing disagree, the drawing is printed and the register is named: the 50 barg cold-box pair is PSV-3560A/B on PR11 and PSV-3562A/B in the register; PSV-3591A/B and PSV-3592 are 10 barg on PR19 against 15 barg in the register, and a relief cannot be set above the 10 barg design of V-359A/B and F-359. 802 manual valves are digitised for this area — 534 of them with no valve type at all. Operation · start-up — manual §8.7.7 · §8.7.8 · Table 8.19 · vendor slides 67–69 · oil pump, then HP, then LP

Start-up — ten permissives, then eight steps

The ten permissives — every one confirmed, or the sequence never starts
aBoth compressor motors in AUTO · C-351L-x and C-351H-x
bLube-oil pump P-351-x in AUTO
cAll oil-cooler fans in AUTO
dBoth capacity slide valves in AUTO
eSuction and discharge isolation confirmed OPEN
fLube-oil temperature in the start range · manual gives no number
gBoth compressors unloaded · slide valve < 5 %
hAll solenoid valves in AUTO
iNo active shutdown, trip or critical alarm on the package
jMotor restart-inhibit / cool-down timers expired
The sequence — Table 8.19 + vendor slides 68 / 69 · and what is actually running at each step
not readyIf any one permissive fails the HMI shows Not ready to start and the sequence is terminated — it does not queue and does not retry. The NO PERM field (PERM TAG / PERM TYPE) names which one. Permissive f has no number in the manual: the vendor pack alone puts 40–60 °C on it.
vendor warningStarting the compressor filled with oil will damage the compressor. The 20-minute wait exists so the oil in the compressor drains back to the oil separator. The manual mentions only a restart-inhibit timer — the number and the reason are vendor-only.
Operation · shutdown — manual §8.7.9 · Table 8.20 · vendor slides 70–72 · LP first, HP second

Shutdown — and the overlap you must not interrupt

The ten steps — five for the LP, then the identical five for the HP · and what is actually running at each one
The overlapone oil circuit, two machines
What is truethe oil pump serves both machines from one inventory (§8.7.5)
During LP post-lubethe HP machine is still running and still being lubricated by the same pump
After the LP stopsthe pump must stay in service for the whole HP half of the sequence
The riskkilling the package between the two stops leaves the HP with no post-lubrication
The rulelet the sequence finish. Package complete is reported only after BOTH machines confirm stopped

Operation · troubleshooting — manual §8.8 Table 8.21 in full · 13 symptoms — ordered by what actually fails

Troubleshooting — symptom, possible cause, what you check first

SymptomPossible causeCheck FIRST — then the manual remedy
Loss of oil differential
PDALL-3514.Lx / .Hx · trip		Pump not developing pressure · oil too cold · lube-oil filter clogged · low level in the separator · pressure switch defective or mis-set · loose contact wiringPDI-3514.Lx / .Hx on the HMI against the 1.5 bar trip, then the two transmitters it is calculated from (PT-3513.x oil header, PT-3512.x discharge) · then PDG-3514.x / PDG-3515.x · then the separator level — remedy: PDCV to 50–60 psid (3.4–4.1 bar) at the regulator inlet · warm the oil in HAND to at least 90 °F (32 °C), suction valve closed · replace the filter · add oil
High oil header temperature
TAHH-3518.Lx / .Hx		High suction temperature · oil cooler not rejecting · heater still energisedE-351-x fans running, and the cooler faces for fouling · then TIC-3517.x and the X-351-x heater — the vendor sheet blames a thermal expansion valve; this circuit has none, so suspect the probe or its control
High discharge temperature
TAHH-3512.Lx / .Hx		Oil injection lost or hot · machine running against a high discharge pressure · suction condition wrongOil temperature and oil flow to that machine first · then PT-3512.x discharge pressure · then TAHH-3519.Lx LP suction temperature
Loss of capacity on one train
slide valve		Slide valve not following · hydraulic oil block valves shut · capacity solenoid not driven · unloaded because a permissive is missingZT-3511.Lx / .Hx position against the load · then the hydraulic oil block valves · then whether the train is the swing train and simply modulating
Falling separator level · seal leakageExcess leakage from the compressor seal · coalescers not tight enough to seal · oil return line from the separator blocked · leaks · oil leaving through a relief valveWalk the shaft seals — it is a daily row on the monitoring schedule · then check all relief-valve discharge piping for oil · tighten the coalescers · adjust or clear the return-line block valve
High oil carryoverCoalescer element loose or badly mountedMount and tighten the coalescer · then the differential across it — the manual asks not less than 0.25 psid, a third figure: use 0.8 barg, conflict A-10
High ΔP across the oil filterOil filter plugged · coalescer drain line chokedLook for oil accumulating in the sight glass and open the globe valve further to restore flow · then change the filter on the standby pair
Bad oil qualitySolids in the oilDrain, refill with clean oil, flush if necessary · have the oil analysed and eliminate the source
Oil pump will not run in HANDOverload open · the compressor is running · main power off · panel control power off · motor burned out · rotation reversedThe pumps must be in AUTO while the compressor runs · reset the overload · check the starter disconnect and the panel control power · check and correct rotation
Oil pump will not run in AUTOCompressor start not initiated · pump not developing enough pressure · oil too cold · rotation reversedInitiate the start sequence · PDCV to 30–60 psid (2.1–4.1 bar) · warm the oil to about 100 °F (38 °C) · correct the rotation
Pump runs in AUTO but the machine will not startLube-oil supply pressure low · motor wired incorrectly · slide valve not < 5 %Confirm fully unloaded and the hydraulic oil block valves open · then PDCV to 30–60 psid · then the motor wiring
Starts, then stops immediatelyStarter or auxiliary contact wired incorrectly · error in the start logicThe auxiliary contact must seal within 3 seconds — a wiring fault there looks exactly like a logic fault; then the start logic
Complete / partial loss of power · abnormal noiseMain disconnect open or main fuse blown · auxiliary fuse or supply · damaged bearings · loose connections · foreign material · misalignment · rotors rubbing the casingPower wiring and fuses · for noise, stop the machine, then the suction strainer and internals, then alignment and coupling

2Why a MIXED refrigerant4 components
  • C1 · C2 · C4 · N₂, watched by chromatograph AT-3581 on the 20″ suction header.
  • A mixture boils over a RANGE of temperature, not at one point.
  • So its cooling curve can follow the gas down.
  • Ammonia alone stops at E-354, near 5 °C. Everything colder is MR expanding inside the cold box.
3Six trains, TWO stages5 + 1
  • C-351L-x + C-351H-x per package · 5 running, 1 standby.
  • Both motors 560 kW, 690 V, VFD — yet LP sweeps 5820 m³/h against 1997 m³/h on the HP.
  • HP suction is not only LP discharge: a 6″ feed comes straight off the package suction.
  • So an LP slide-valve move changes HP suction composition, not just flow.
4Oil is the machine≥ 1.5 bar D
  • One inventory, one separator V-351-x, one cooler E-351-x (10 fans), one pump P-351-x (4 kW)…
  • …but TWO separate loops and FOUR filters F-351-xA/B/C/D — A/B on the pumped HP bearing loop, C/D on the unpumped loop feeding both machines.
  • PDI-3514.Lx/.Hx is CALCULATED in the PLC: PT-3513.x − PT-3512.x.
  • Below 1.5 bar D the machine will not start and will not keep running.
5The cold box is not openedno field repair
  • E-356A and E-356B are brazed-aluminium plate-fin cores inside CB-356: no internal drawing, no field repair.
  • What keeps oil out of the MR passes is oil removal S-352 — coalescers V-352-1/2 (15 cartridges each), charcoal V-352-3/4, filters F-352A/B.
  • Oil that gets past S-352 does not come back out.
6Capacity controlN−1 + swing
  • Two modes on one master pair, picked on the HMI overview: XC-3501B flow mode (FIC-3560A) or XC-3501A superheat mode. Same set point either way.
  • How many trains run is a MANUAL decision (§8.4). The control system trims; it does not choose the machine count.
  • The rest sit at full load; the swing train modulates its slide valve through PIC-3511.Hx.
  • Below its turndown, XC-3501A opens hot-gas bypass PV-3581 back to V-358.
7When a train trips2 moves
  • §8.4 gives the operator exactly two: start another train, or cut the natural-gas feed rate. There is no third option.
  • Start HP first, LP second; stop LP first, HP second — the machine that starts last stops first, so the LP stage never compresses into a stopped HP stage.
  • 30 s post-lubrication after every stop.
  • Twelve machine trips LSD09…LSD20 · PSD02 = loss of the MR loop, where Unit 340 had PSD01.
